result.summary: The environment is a residential street with incomplete pedestrian infrastructure, featuring a sidewalk on only one side and no marked crossings. The wide, unmarked roadway and frequent driveway curb cuts create a space where pedestrians are poorly separated from vehicular traffic.

hazards.name: Missing sidewalk
hazards.description: The left side of the street lacks a paved walkway, forcing pedestrians into the roadway or onto uneven grass.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the residential frontage.

hazards.name: Wide unmarked roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings and the overall width of the street may encourage higher vehicle speeds in a residential area.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, the main travel way.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked areas for pedestrians to cross the street safely.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the visible roadway.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Install a continuous paved sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a safe, dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install speed humps or other vertical traffic calming measures to reduce vehicle speeds on this wide residential street.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Mark crossings with high-visibility paint to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a continuous sidewalk separated from the roadway by a grass buffer. While the environment is generally low-speed, the sidewalk shows signs of wear and there is a lack of formal crossing infrastructure.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb can block the view of pedestrians, particularly children, from oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right side of the roadway.

hazards.name: Degraded sidewalk surface
hazards.description: Cracks and vegetation growth in the sidewalk joints create uneven surfaces that may pose a trip hazard.
hazards.location_in_image: The sidewalk running parallel to the road in the foreground.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair
interventions.description: Repair the cracked sidewalk to provide a smooth and accessible surface for all users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians and reduce crossing distances.

result.summary: This residential street features a buffered sidewalk on one side but lacks a continuous walkway on the opposite side, where driveways dominate the frontage. The wide, unmarked roadway and absence of formal crossing infrastructure create a environment that prioritizes vehicle movement over pedestrian connectivity.

hazards.name: Discontinuous sidewalk
hazards.description: The right side of the street lacks a continuous paved walkway, forcing pedestrians to walk in the roadway or across private driveways.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway in front of the brick houses

hazards.name: Wide unmarked roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a relatively wide street can encourage higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable positioning.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the asphalt roadway

hazards.name: Multiple driveway conflict points
hazards.description: Frequent curb cuts for residential parking increase the number of points where vehicles may cross the pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street along the residential frontage

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a continuous sidewalk on the right side of the street to provide a safe, dedicated space for pedestrians on both sides.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or speed cushions to manage vehicle speeds in this residential context.

interventions.title: Lane Markings
interventions.description: Add center line or edge line markings to narrow the perceived travel lanes and organize traffic flow.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street environment that lacks any dedicated pedestrian infrastructure, such as sidewalks or marked crossings. Pedestrians are forced to share the roadway with vehicles, and the presence of informal 'Please Slow Down' signs suggests a perceived safety issue regarding vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalks
hazards.description: There is no paved walkway for pedestrians, forcing them to walk in the street or on the grass.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the visible roadway edges

hazards.name: Lack of Street Lighting
hazards.description: No street lights are visible, which significantly reduces pedestrian safety and visibility at night.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the street frontage

hazards.name: Informal Speed Warnings
hazards.description: The presence of yard signs asking drivers to slow down indicates a resident-perceived hazard of speeding vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: On the grass verge in the foreground

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a continuous paved sidewalk on at least one side of the street to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install standard street lighting to improve visibility for all road users during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement physical traffic calming such as speed humps or a neighborhood traffic circle to naturally reduce vehicle speeds.
